The issue of mode collapse in GANs is a significant challenge in image generation, and we propose a novel approach to diagnose and mitigate it. By analyzing the Hessian matrix of the generator's loss function, we can identify and rank the importance of each image feature. Our method, Hessian-guided GAN training, leverages this analysis to develop a loss function that encourages the generator to produce more diverse images. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in generating high-quality images with reduced mode collapse. Furthermore, our analysis of the Hessian matrix reveals that the generator's loss landscape is highly irregular, and we provide a theoretical explanation for this phenomenon. By leveraging the fact that the interior point method's residual decreases monotonically, we can terminate the inner iterations once the residual falls below a predetermined threshold. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through numerical experiments on large-scale linear and nonlinear optimization problems. This suggests that the proposed early stopping strategy can be a valuable tool for solving large-scale optimization problems. Furthermore, our results indicate that the proposed early stopping strategy can be integrated with other interior point methods to further improve their efficiency. This is particularly promising, as it may enable the development of more efficient interior point methods in the future. Finally, we discuss potential avenues for future research in this area. The proposed learnable MFCCs are designed to be used in conjunction with a deep neural network (DNN) for speaker verification tasks. Furthermore, our learnable MFCCs also exhibit improved performance when compared to traditional MFCCs in speaker diarization, achieving a 10.4% reduction in diarization error rate (DER) on the AMI meeting corpus. The phenomenon of emotion contagion, where people unconsciously adopt others' emotions, is a widespread occurrence in everyday life. Conversely, consuming positive content has a minimal effect on contagion, and consuming content with neutral sentiment has no discernible effect. We also found that users who are more emotionally expressive are more susceptible to contagion, and our analysis suggests that contagion is more likely to occur when people are exposed to content that is emotionally similar to their own. These findings have implications for the spread of negative emotions, such as anxiety and depression, and highlight the potential for social media to exacerbate these issues. Ultimately, our research underscores the importance of developing effective strategies to mitigate the spread of negative emotions on social media. Furthermore, we provide a detailed analysis of the characteristics of rare errors and their distribution within the dataset. Our research suggests that the rarity of errors should be taken into account when evaluating GEC systems, and we recommend using our method to create a more comprehensive evaluation set. Our findings suggest that SSIoT is a promising solution for IoT applications that require secure, decentralized, and efficient data management. Specifically, we prove that the degree of a Galois covering is a positive integer, and that the ramification indices of such coverings exhibit multiplicative behavior. The LHCb experiment at CERN is preparing to upgrade its detector for Run 3, 
which will significantly increase data transfer rates to 3.5 terabytes per second.
To meet this challenge, a real-time data filtering system is being developed to 
process data at the source, reducing the amount of data sent to CERN for analysis.
This paper presents a novel approach to designing a graph network that can handle 
the increased data volume while meeting strict latency requirements.
The proposed network utilizes a distance-weighted metric to prioritize data 
transmission based on the likelihood of subsequent processing steps.
This approach is compared to a traditional graph network and demonstrated to be 
effective in reducing data volume and latency on a real-world dataset from the 
LHCb experiment. The results show that the distance-weighted network can achieve a 
reduction of up to 90% in data volume and a 50% reduction in latency. 
Furthermore, the network's performance is scalable, allowing it to handle 
increasing data volumes while maintaining a constant latency. 
This approach is expected to be a key component of the LHCb experiment's real-time 
data filtering system.

By utilizing a distance metric based on the Euclidean distance between the last layer weights of two architectures, we can efficiently calculate the pairwise distances between a large number of architectures. Our approach involves a two-stage process: first, we calculate the pairwise distances between a subset of architectures, and then we use these distances to estimate the pairwise distances between the remaining architectures. This method is particularly useful for analyzing large datasets of neural networks, as it can reduce the computational cost by a factor of 10 to 100 times. To demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, we applied it to a large dataset of 1.5 million neural networks and achieved a significant reduction in computational cost. Our results show that this method can efficiently calculate the pairwise distances between a large number of architectures, making it a valuable tool for analyzing neural network efficiency. Physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) have been successfully applied to solve various partial differential equations (PDEs) by leveraging the power of deep learning. However, the performance of PINNs is often limited by the complexity of the problems they are trying to solve. In this study, we investigate the performance of PINNs on increasingly complex problems, such as the Poisson equation, the heat equation, and the Schrödinger equation, by gradually increasing the number of equations, the time domain size, and the spatial dimension. Our results show that the performance of PINNs deteriorates as the complexity of the problems increases, and we observe that the performance decline is more pronounced when increasing the time domain size compared to increasing the number of equations or spatial dimension. Furthermore, we find that the performance decline is more significant when solving time-dependent PDEs compared to time-independent PDEs. Our findings are supported by numerical experiments and provide valuable insights for the practical application of PINNs. This paper introduces Gemino, a novel video codec that leverages the benefits of both intra and inter frame coding to enhance video quality at low bitrates. Building upon the intra frame coding capabilities of AV1, Gemino incorporates inter frame coding to capture motion between frames. To address the challenges of motion estimation, Gemino employs a hierarchical block-based approach, utilizing a coarse-to-fine framework to estimate motion. The proposed codec also features a motion vector field refinement module, which significantly improves video quality at low bitrates. Experimental results demonstrate that Gemino outperforms AV1 by 0.3-0.5 dB in PSNR and 0.2-0.3 dB in SSIM, while achieving a 10-20% reduction in bitrate. Moreover, Gemino's efficiency is further validated by its superior performance in YUV444 and YUV420 formats, outdoing AV1 by 0.5-0.7 dB in PSNR and 0.3-0.4 dB in SSIM. In this research, we introduce a novel approach to garment manipulation that
builds upon existing methods, enhancing their performance. Our technique
involves a policy that adjusts the garment's position in relation to the
manipulator, taking into account the object's pose and the hand's position.
This policy is trained using a dataset of simulated scenarios, where the
object's pose is known, and the hand's position is provided. Our results show
that this method surpasses the performance of a basic manually-designed
garment manipulation technique, even when applied to real-world situations
where the object's pose is unknown. Furthermore, we demonstrate that our
approach can be integrated with a separate pose estimation system to achieve
even better results. Our code and dataset are publicly available for review. 
The accompanying video provides a visual representation of the technique's
capabilities.

To address this issue, we propose a novel approach called OPG, which generates pseudo-unseen samples by leveraging the differences between seen and unseen classes. Specifically, OPG first identifies the most distinctive features of seen classes and then uses these features to create pseudo-unseen samples. By doing so, OPG effectively simulates the differences between seen and unseen classes, leading to improved performance on unseen classes. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, which outperforms existing methods in one-shot novel class detection.
